requirements.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster established and healthy before maintenance
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster, node2 and node3 joined via systemctl start; wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced confirmed on node1 with all three incoming addresses listed.

requirements.requirement: Application data present and replicated across all members before the outage
requirements.summary: appdb.orders created and populated on node1, identical rows confirmed via direct query on node2 and node3, and a distinct pre-maintenance-marker row inserted on node2 and read back, demonstrating multi-directional replication.

requirements.requirement: Cluster brought down completely for the maintenance window
requirements.summary: mariadb was stopped on node1, node2, and node3 in turn, with systemctl is-active returning 'inactive' on each node after its stop, directly demonstrating a full-cluster outage.

requirements.requirement: Correct bootstrap source identified after the outage using Galera state (not just arbitrary restart)
requirements.summary: grastate.dat was inspected on all three nodes post-outage; node3 held the highest seqno (9) with safe_to_bootstrap=1, and it was the node used to bootstrap the resumed cluster, matching Galera's safe-recovery procedure.

requirements.requirement: Cluster brought back with every committed write present and all three members serving again
requirements.summary: node3 was bootstrapped, node1 and node2 rejoined; wsrep_cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced was confirmed on all three nodes, and appdb.orders (including the pre-maintenance marker row) was verified present on node1, node2, and node3.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart protocol: node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: node1 baseline boot_id 73237116... and healthy cluster_size=3 captured; systemctl reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id 838861a0... confirmed changed (also cross-checked against fixed after_executor snapshot); mariadb (found disabled) was restarted and enabled, and cluster_size=3/Synced plus intact data were confirmed before proceeding.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart protocol: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: node2 baseline boot_id 434803ac... captured; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id f6828c8d... confirmed changed (matches fixed after_executor snapshot); mariadb auto-started (previously enabled) and cluster_size=3/Synced plus intact data confirmed.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart protocol: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: node3 baseline boot_id 254597f8... captured; reboot acked; post-reboot boot_id a415c4c3... confirmed changed (matches fixed after_executor snapshot); mariadb auto-started and cluster_size=3/Synced plus intact data confirmed.

requirements.requirement: Final confirmation all three members serving after full restart cycle
requirements.summary: A new write issued on node3 (widget-post-restart-check) was independently confirmed present on node1 and node2 with wsrep_cluster_size=3 on both, directly demonstrating all three members serving and replicating post-restart.

overall_summary: The executor stood up a fresh 3-node Galera cluster, verified pre-maintenance data replication, executed a genuine full-cluster outage, correctly used grastate.dat seqno comparison to pick the safe bootstrap node (node3, seqno 9, safe_to_bootstrap=1) rather than an arbitrary one, and directly demonstrated recovery of all committed writes with all three members Synced. It then completed the mandatory per-node restart evidence protocol with baseline/ack/changed-boot-id/recovered-state proof for each node, cross-checked against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots, and closed with a live cross-node write/read check confirming all three members serving. All material task outcomes and the restart protocol are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence; hygiene is high with only trivial leftover install logs as residue.
limitations: Evidence is limited to captured command stdout/exit codes; no independent verification of underlying replication internals (e.g., wsrep GTID states) beyond the status variables and row-level checks shown.

The full-cluster outage and restart-per-node sequencing were sequential rather than simultaneous, which is normal operational practice but means there is no single snapshot showing all three nodes down or all three mid-reboot at once.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command timeline; nearly all state-changing actions map directly to task prerequisites (package install, /etc/hosts entries, firewalld port openings, galera.cnf authoring, cluster bootstrap/join, data writes, controlled stop/start, restart protocol, service enablement). The one failed dnf install on node1 (cmd-d9b22ae753ea4a01/cmd-fb5b78a9afa24832) due to a GPG key parsing error was a legitimate corrective retry (cmd-bb190a9b395f447f), not an unnecessary mutation. Enabling mariadb for autostart on all three nodes (cmd-1539899dadad4216, cmd-67e93b2ed7314f72, cmd-1d2000cf22ed4545) was a reasonable prerequisite for the restart-recovery protocol, since node1 was found disabled post-reboot. The only residue is minor and low-risk: /tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid (and /tmp/install2.log on node1) were left behind on all three nodes per the after_executor temporary-files diff; this is inert installation-log residue with no functional or security impact and does not warrant a lower score.
